title: Meet Japan's 90-Year-Old Bodybuilding Champion
paragraphs: Most people would probably see their 90th birthday as a good time to slow down. But Toshisuke Kanazawa celebrated his by winning his 19th national bodybuilding title.
On August 30, just one day after his 90th birthday, Kanazawa beat seven other men in the over-85 group at the Japan Masters Bodybuilding Championships in Hiroshima.

Kanazawa's dream of becoming a champion goes back many years. Born in Shimane prefecture in 1936, as a young man, he told his parents that he wanted to become the best bodybuilder in Japan. His father thought he should get a job instead, but Kanazawa asked his father to give him a few years to achieve his goal.
Kanazawa spent five years training six hours a day. That hard work paid off when, in 1960, aged 24, he became Mr. Japan. Three years later, he won the title again.
His success didn't stop there, either — in 1967, Kanazawa entered the Mr. Universe competition in Montreal, Canada, and finished fourth.
Kanazawa retired from bodybuilding in his mid-30s, but returned at 50 to inspire his wife, who had been sick for a long time.
Today, Kanazawa trains for two hours a day, six days a week. He can't train in the same way he used to — he no longer does squats or bench presses, and his body takes longer to recover, he says.
But for Kanazawa, getting older just means changing how he trains, not giving up something he loves.
"Older Japanese people are doing incredible things, but I worry that too many of them give up on the things they did when they were younger," he told The Guardian.
Kanazawa has followed that idea himself. At 90, he's still competing — and doesn't plan to stop.
"I want to be a bodybuilder until the day I die," he said.
